name: Greenish hunter green
lede: Greenish hunter green is ColorHub's name for Aoni (青丹), a traditional Japanese color whose name, "blue-black clay," reflects an older sense of *ao* spanning blue, green and grey.

sections.title: Aoni, blue-black clay
sections.body:
Our library lists this color under the Japanese name Aoni, written 青丹, glossed as "blue-black clay" [1]. In older Japanese, *ao* covers a wider span than modern "blue," reaching into greens and greys, which is why a clay-based name lands on a green swatch here [1]. No book consulted independently dates the name beyond the library's gloss, so its coinage is undocumented here [1].

The swatch measures lightness 36, chroma 19 and hue 117 degrees, in the Greens family, and the library's nearest fashion neighbor is [[new-hay]] [1]. At 9.8 units from [[hunter-green]] it is a visible but moderate shift, used chiefly in fashion and textile contexts [1]. A greyer version of the same base name, [[greyish-hunter-green]], sits darker and less saturated.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: A color within range of this swatch appears in 1,005 of the 23,781 paintings in our archive, about 4.2 percent, as photographed, roughly evenly split between mid-tone and shadow use [2]. The earliest dated match is a 1190 painting attributed to Wu Bing, *Bamboo and Insects*, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. Henri Rousseau carries it in 6 of 13 dated paintings, 10.9 times the archive's overall rate [2]. The archive's photographs are of aged, varnished canvases, so a match is a screen color near this one, not a pigment identification [2].

origin.named_after: 青 (ao), blue/green, + 丹 (ni), clay or red earth
